summary: This note introduces a Wikipedia list of territorial entities where English holds official-language status, defined as a language used in citizen interactions with government officials. It states that in 2015 there were 54 sovereign states and 27 non-sovereign entities with English as an official language. It also notes that many country subdivisions have declared English official at local or regional levels.
one_line: Wikipedia introduction to a list of sovereign states and non-sovereign territories where English is an official language.
key_facts: The list covers territories where English is an official language, defined as a language used in citizen interactions with government officials.
In 2015, there were 54 sovereign states where English was an official language.
In 2015, there were 27 non-sovereign entities where English was an official language.
Many country subdivisions have declared English an official language at the local or regional level.
